Written with the intention of inspiring young minds, the book urges students to rise above limitations, embrace rationality, and pursue education as a tool of liberation.</span></p><p></p><p><span>Ambedkar emphasizes that true progress begins with awareness—awareness of one’s rights, responsibilities, and potential. Through his sharp insights, he guides learners to cultivate discipline, critical thinking, moral courage, and an unshakeable commitment to social justice.</span></p><p></p><p><span>The book stands as a motivational call for every student to become conscious, confident, and socially responsible. It is not just a message about education, but about building character, asserting dignity, and shaping a more equal society.</span></p><p></p><p><span>Ideal for students, educators, and readers interested in Ambedkar’s philosophy, this work remains a timeless reminder that education is the doorway to empowerment and transformation.</span></p><p><br></p>

products.title: The Buddha and his Dhamma
products.subtitle: (English)
products.descriptionHtml: <p><span>“The Buddha and His Dhamma” is Dr. B. R. Ambedkar’s monumental reinterpretation of the life and teachings of Buddha, written with a modern, rational, and socially conscious perspective. Unlike traditional religious commentaries, Ambedkar presents Buddhism not as a mystical faith, but as an ethical and practical guide for building a just society.</span></p><p></p><p><span>A deeply significant part of Ambedkar’s analysis is his rejection of Mayavada—the Advaita Vedanta doctrine that the world is an illusion (maya). In this book, Ambedkar argues that such philosophies weaken social responsibility by denying the reality of human suffering. He contrasts this with the Buddha’s teachings, which treat the world, pain, and social injustice as real and demanding practical action.</span></p><p></p><p><span>Through clear narration and critical reasoning, Ambedkar shows:</span></p><p></p><ul><li><p><span>Buddhism as a religion of reason, equality, and compassion</span></p></li><li><p><span>The Buddha’s rejection of metaphysical speculation, including the idea that life is mere illusion</span></p></li><li><p><span>The Dhamma as a path of moral responsibility, social awareness, and liberation from oppression</span></p></li><li><p><span>Why Ambedkar chose Buddhism as a movement for human dignity and social transformation</span></p></li></ul><p></p><p></p><p><span>This book is both a biography of the Buddha and a philosophical text that sharpens the difference between Buddhist ethics and Mayavada’s emphasis on illusion and detachment.</span></p><p></p><p><span>Profound, historically grounded, and socially revolutionary, The Buddha and His Dhamma remains Ambedkar’s definitive contribution to modern Buddhist thought and a guiding text for anyone seeking truth through reason and justice.</span></p><p><br></p>

products.title: Shudra Purvi Kaun Hote ?
products.subtitle: Written by Dr.B.R.Ambedkar
products.descriptionHtml: <p>In <a rel="noopener noreferrer nofollow" href="https://www.google.co.in/search?q=Who+Were+the+Shudras%3F&client=safari&sca_esv=ea4088b713ffc869&hl=en-in&ei=xVYlaeaoJveX4-EP5PP38Ag&oq=discription+for+the+book+who+were+the+shudras+by+B+R%C2%A0&gs_-QEYjAXYAQHCAgcQABiABBgNwgIKEAAYgAQYsQMYDcICBhAAGA0YHsICBhAAGBYYHsICCBAAGAUYDRgewgILEAAYgAQYhgMYigXCAggQABiABBiiBMICBRAAGO8FwgIFECEYnwXCAggQABiiBBiJBcICBBAhGBWYAwLxBdmNSuKI4y7JiAYBkAYIugYECAEYCpIHCjIxLjQ2LjE3LjGgB62IA7IHCTEuNDYuMTcuMbgHwV3CBwkxLjkuNjAuMTXIB5cD&sclient=mobile-gws-wiz-serp&mstk=AUtExfA0yqE6BwcRh7e7aN-hwMP4DK1xSpBHcS0_0XKgbU8QGpVJqeOYFNJrdWck7Eh2Xs5hoql4CtN2Qxo91BUAZtWLqKakjVTWuIjffQb7imkkDxq1FNgH3SmFztu3TGOuE9s&csui=3&ved=2ahUKEwi7kMWL4IyRAxUJ1zgGHbtsAK0QgK4QegQIARAD"><em>Who Were the Shudras?</em></a>, B.R. Ambedkar investigates the origins of the Shudra caste, arguing they were originally Aryan kings who were demoted to a lower caste after a conflict with the Brahmans. The book, dedicated to <a rel="noopener noreferrer nofollow" href="https://www.google.co.in/search?q=Jyotirao+Phule&client=safari&sca_esv=ea4088b713ffc869&hl=en-in&ei=xVYlaeaoJveX4-EP5PP38Ag&oq=discription+for+the+book+who+were+the+shudras+by+B+R%C2%A0&gs_-QEYjAXYAQHCAgcQABiABBgNwgIKEAAYgAQYsQMYDcICBhAAGA0YHsICBhAAGBYYHsICCBAAGAUYDRgewgILEAAYgAQYhgMYigXCAggQABiABBiiBMICBRAAGO8FwgIFECEYnwXCAggQABiiBBiJBcICBBAhGBWYAwLxBdmNSuKI4y7JiAYBkAYIugYECAEYCpIHCjIxLjQ2LjE3LjGgB62IA7IHCTEuNDYuMTcuMbgHwV3CBwkxLjkuNjAuMTXIB5cD&sclient=mobile-gws-wiz-serp&mstk=AUtExfA0yqE6BwcRh7e7aN-hwMP4DK1xSpBHcS0_0XKgbU8QGpVJqeOYFNJrdWck7Eh2Xs5hoql4CtN2Qxo91BUAZtWLqKakjVTWuIjffQb7imkkDxq1FNgH3SmFztu3TGOuE9s&csui=3&ved=2ahUKEwi7kMWL4IyRAxUJ1zgGHbtsAK0QgK4QegQIARAE">Jyotirao Phule</a>, uses Indian scriptures like the Vedas and Mahabharata to challenge the myth that Shudras were inherently an untouchable caste. Ambedkar also analyzes and rejects the popular <a rel="noopener noreferrer nofollow" href="https://www.google.co.in/search?q=Indo-Aryan+migration+theory&client=safari&sca_esv=ea4088b713ffc869&hl=en-in&ei=xVYlaeaoJveX4-EP5PP38Ag&oq=discription+for+the+book+who+were+the+shudras+by+B+R%C2%A0&gs_-QEYjAXYAQHCAgcQABiABBgNwgIKEAAYgAQYsQMYDcICBhAAGA0YHsICBhAAGBYYHsICCBAAGAUYDRgewgILEAAYgAQYhgMYigXCAggQABiABBiiBMICBRAAGO8FwgIFECEYnwXCAggQABiiBBiJBcICBBAhGBWYAwLxBdmNSuKI4y7JiAYBkAYIugYECAEYCpIHCjIxLjQ2LjE3LjGgB62IA7IHCTEuNDYuMTcuMbgHwV3CBwkxLjkuNjAuMTXIB5cD&sclient=mobile-gws-wiz-serp&mstk=AUtExfA0yqE6BwcRh7e7aN-hwMP4DK1xSpBHcS0_0XKgbU8QGpVJqeOYFNJrdWck7Eh2Xs5hoql4CtN2Qxo91BUAZtWLqKakjVTWuIjffQb7imkkDxq1FNgH3SmFztu3TGOuE9s&csui=3&ved=2ahUKEwi7kMWL4IyRAxUJ1zgGHbtsAK0QgK4QegQIARAF">Indo-Aryan migration theory</a>, offering a historical argument for the subjugation of the Shudra varna.<span> </span></p><ul><li><p>Argues Shudras were originally Brahmins: Ambedkar contends that the Shudras were not originally a separate, low-caste group, but were rather Aryans who were later relegated to a lower social standing after a conflict with Brahmans.</p></li><li><p>Uses ancient texts as evidence: The book draws on and interprets ancient Indian scriptures, such as the Vedas and Mahabharata, to support its historical claims.</p></li><li><p>Debunks myths: It seeks to dispel common misconceptions about the Shudra caste, particularly the idea that they are an "untouchable" caste.</p></li><li><p>Critiques the Indo-Aryan theory:Ambedkar also analyzes the Aryan race theory and the Indo-Aryan migration theory, disagreeing with the prevailing narrative of the time.</p></li><li><p>Call for social reform: The book is a significant contribution to the study of caste and social justice, highlighting the need for social reform and equality</p></li></ul><p></p><p></p><p>The book is available in Hindi,English and Marathi language.</p><p></p>

products.title: The Problem Of Rupee
products.subtitle: Written by- Dr. B.R.Ambedkar
products.descriptionHtml: <p><span><strong>The Problem of the Rupee: Its Origin and Its Solution</strong></span></p><p><span>-by Dr. B. R. Ambedkar</span></p><p></p><p><span>The Problem of the Rupee is Dr. B. R. Ambedkar’s groundbreaking study of India’s monetary history, currency systems, and financial instability under British rule. First published in 1923, this classic work examines how flawed economic policies—particularly the silver standard and the gold exchange standard—shaped the value of the Indian rupee and affected the country’s economy.</span></p><p></p><p><span>Ambedkar traces the evolution of the rupee from ancient times to the colonial period, critically analyzing the decisions that led to inflation, currency depreciation, and structural economic imbalance. Using sharp economic reasoning, he exposes how British monetary policy prioritized imperial interests over India’s financial stability.</span></p><p></p><p><span>Key themes of the book include:</span></p><p></p><ul><li><p><span>Historical origin of the Indian rupee and its changing standards</span></p></li><li><p><span>Ambedkar’s critique of the silver and gold exchange systems</span></p></li><li><p><span>The impact of British monetary policies on Indian trade and prices</span></p></li><li><p><span>The need for a sound, stable, and autonomous monetary system</span></p></li><li><p><span>His persuasive argument for adopting the gold standard and establishing a central bank</span></p></li></ul><p></p><p></p><p><span>Ambedkar’s recommendations in this book directly influenced the formation of the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) in 1935, making the work one of the most important economic texts in modern Indian history.</span></p><p></p><p><span>Clear, analytical, and deeply insightful, The Problem of the Rupee remains essential reading for students of economics, history, public policy, and anyone interested in understanding the foundations of India’s financial system.</span></p>

products.title: Savitribai Phule
products.subtitle: Written by Indira Ukey
products.descriptionHtml: <p><span>In a time when educating a girl was seen as an act of rebellion, Savitribai Phule stepped forward to ignite a revolution. Born into a society bound by rigid caste rules and gender injustice, she dared to dream of a world where every child could learn, question, and rise. With unwavering resolve—and alongside her visionary partner </span><span style="color: rgb(0, 0, 238);">Jyotirao Phule</span><span>—she opened India’s first school for girls, becoming the nation’s first female teacher and its most fearless advocate for equality.</span></p><p></p><p><span>This biography brings to life her relentless fight against oppression: from confronting violent opposition to challenging caste hierarchies, championing widow remarriage, and standing with the most marginalized. Through resilience, compassion, and radical vision, Savitribai reshaped India’s social and educational landscape forever.</span></p><p></p><p><span>A story of extraordinary courage, Savitribai Phule – The Courage to Educate is not just a chronicle of one woman’s life—it is a reminder of how a single voice, determined and daring, can spark a movement that transforms generations.</span></p><p><br></p>

products.title: Sant Kabir -Jeevan Charitra
products.subtitle: written by Suryakant Bhagat
products.descriptionHtml: <p><span><strong>Sant Kabir – Voice of Truth, Light of Humanity</strong></span></p><p></p><p></p><p><span>In an age divided by caste, creed, and ritual, Sant Kabir emerged as a fearless poet-saint whose words cut through illusion and awakened a society lost in dogma. Born into humble circumstances and raised by the compassionate weavers </span><span style="color: rgb(0, 0, 238);">Niru and Nima</span><span>, Kabir transformed the simple threads of daily life into timeless verses of spiritual wisdom. His powerful dohas challenged empty rituals, exposed social injustice, and illuminated the path of love, equality, and inner awakening.</span></p><p></p><p><span>This biography journeys through Kabir’s extraordinary life—his fearless stand against religious orthodoxy, his message of a formless divine, his rejection of caste barriers, and his ability to unite Hindus and Muslims through the universal language of truth. With clarity, courage, and compassion, Kabir’s voice rose above divisions, echoing a message still urgently relevant today.</span></p><p></p><p><span>Sant Kabir – Voice of Truth, Light of Humanity brings alive the mystic weaver whose words continue to inspire seekers, challenge injustice, and remind us that the ultimate journey is inward. A life beyond legend, a legacy beyond time—Kabir remains the saint who taught the world to see with the eyes of the soul.</span></p><p></p>

products.title: Samrat Ashoka
products.subtitle: Written by Suryakant Bhagat
products.descriptionHtml: <p><span><strong>Samrat Ashok – From Conqueror to Compassion</strong></span></p><p></p><p></p><p><span>In the vast expanse of ancient India, few rulers shaped history as profoundly as Samrat Ashok—the monarch who transformed an empire and redefined the meaning of power. Born into the mighty </span><span style="color: rgb(0, 0, 238);">Maurya Empire</span><span>, he rose from a fierce warrior and strategic conqueror to become one of the world’s greatest champions of peace.</span></p><p></p><p><span>This biography traces his riveting journey: the battles that forged his early reign, the monumental conquest of Kalinga that shook his conscience, and the extraordinary spiritual awakening that followed. Renouncing violence, he embraced the path of Dharma and spread the teachings of compassion, tolerance, and moral governance across his vast kingdom and beyond.</span></p><p></p><p><span>Through stone edicts, public reforms, and a visionary commitment to human welfare, he reshaped the idea of kingship—proving that true strength lies not in the sword, but in the service of humanity.</span></p><p></p><p><span>Samrat Ashok – From Conqueror to Compassion brings alive the story of a ruler who rose above his time, leaving a legacy that continues to inspire the modern world. A tale of power, transformation, and timeless wisdom—this is the life of a king who became a legend.</span></p><p><br></p>

products.title: Pakistan And The Partition of India
products.subtitle: Written by Dr.B.R.Ambedkar (Available in Hindi ,English and Marathi)
products.descriptionHtml: <p><span><strong>Pakistan and the Partition of India</strong></span></p><p></p><p></p><p><span>The Partition of India in 1947 stands as one of the most defining—and devastating—turning points in South Asian history. As British colonial rule under </span><span style="color: rgb(0, 0, 238);">British Empire</span><span> drew to an end, rising political tensions, communal mistrust, and competing national visions reshaped the destiny of millions. The demand for a separate homeland, articulated strongly by the </span><span style="color: rgb(0, 0, 238);">All-India Muslim League</span><span>, and negotiations with the leaders of the </span><span style="color: rgb(0, 0, 238);">Indian National Congress</span><span> culminated in the creation of Pakistan and the division of the Indian subcontinent.</span></p><p></p><p><span>This biography of events takes readers through the intense political debates, the emotional struggles of common people, and the tragic human cost of one of the largest mass migrations in world history. It captures the hopes for freedom, the fears of a divided land, and the painful realities that followed—violence, displacement, and the irreversible reshaping of borders and identities.</span></p><p></p><p><span>Pakistan and the Partition of India is not just a chronicle of political decisions; it is the story of a subcontinent torn between unity and separation, faith and fear, trauma and transformation. It reveals how the echoes of 1947 continue to influence India, Pakistan, and the world even today.</span></p>
